key_insight: EventHub is a "data factory" that enables training high-performance event-based stereo networks without costly active sensors by synthesizing proxy events and annotations from ordinary color image datasets. This lets existing RGB stereo models be repurposed for event data using scalable, inexpensive supervision.
problem_solved: Event-based stereo learning depends on expensive, hard-to-scale active sensors or dense ground truth; EventHub removes that dependency by generating training signals from standard color images, making event-stereo training practical and generalizable.
method: Generate training sets from color-image collections by producing proxy annotations and, when needed, proxy events using state-of-the-art novel view synthesis / rendering techniques or by using paired image+event data when available.
Use the synthesized proxy labels/events to supervise event-based stereo networks, allowing re-use of mature RGB stereo architectures adapted to event inputs.
Train and validate models on the generated dataset to achieve generalizable event-stereo performance without collecting active-sensor ground truth.
impact: EventHub drastically lowers the barrier to build and scale event-based stereo models by removing the need for active-sensor ground truth, enabling broader research, faster iteration, and easier domain transfer for neuromorphic and low-latency vision systems.

paper_title: EventHub: Data Factory for Generalizable Event-Based Stereo Networks without Active Sensors
paper_authors: Luca Bartolomei, Fabio Tosi, Matteo Poggi, Stefano Mattoccia, Guillermo Gallego
